## Added

- `render --format webp` writes WebP instead of PNG, with the same result
  shape (only the files differ: `<stem>_page_<n>.webp`). A page without
  raster images (`contains_images: false`) is written lossless, pixel-identical
  to the PNG; a page with them is written lossy at quality 90. On 12 pages of
  three local documents at `--scale-long-edge-px 3200`, text pages came to
  189–342 KB and pages with photographs or maps to 239–996 KB, against
  377–5040 KB as PNG, in 0.1–0.4 s per page. `png` stays the default.

  The encoder is libwebp 1.6.0 (through the `webpx` crate), compiled from
  source into the binary: no new library ships beside it, but building now
  needs a C compiler, which both release runners already have. Its BSD licence
  and patent grant ship in the archive's new `licenses/` directory.

- `render --scale-long-edge-px <N>` sizes the page's longer side to exactly
  `N` pixels — the width of a landscape page, the height of a portrait one —
  and preserves the aspect ratio, like Poppler's `pdftoppm -scale-to`. It
  conflicts with `--scale` and `--scale-width-px`, and the result reports
  `scale_long_edge_px` in their place. Until now a caller wanting one bound
  for mixed sheets had to inspect every page and pick a width per orientation;
  at scale 4 an A1 sheet (2384 pt wide) renders 9536 px wide.

## Changed

- Rendered PNGs are about half the size. They were written at the PNG
  encoder's `Fast` level and as RGBA although every page is drawn onto opaque
  white; they are now written at its `Default` level and as RGB. On a US
  letter text page at 2448×3168 the file went from 1222 KB to 649 KB for ~50 ms
  more encoding; on photo-heavy pages the gain is smaller (4376 KB to
  2580 KB). The pixels are unchanged. A caller that assumed an alpha channel
  gets 3-channel RGB now.
